messages:
maria-support: FYI — multiple support tickets opened this morning reporting large p95/p99 regressions after the v2026.3 runtime canary. Customers on /v1/generate see p95 jump from ~2s to ~4.5s and p99s to ~9s. Sample req IDs: r-8f3b2, r-8f3b9, r-8f4aa. Issues start ~2351234500. Putting details here so eng-runtime + SRE can triage.
deploy-bot: deploy v2026.3 -> canary (20% traffic) succeeded at 2351234400. Image: redwood/runtime:v2026.3
aj-runtime: noted. Is this strictly the canary pool or are we seeing impact on stable? Any cross-pool routing? Also which model(s) affected — large context vs short? 
maria-support: All reports are on hosted (us-west1) canary pool. Models: mostly our 70B variants and some 13B when long context > 2k tokens. Short context calls appear fine. 
leo-sre: quick checks to run: 1) queue depth / hotpath latencies on canary AP pods 2) GPU waveform (stall/SM utilization) 3) kernel selection heatmap (did new kernels land in v2026.3?) 4) cache hit/miss for KV cache. I'll start pulling metrics now.
emma-oncall: If it's strictly the canary, we should drop canary traffic back to 0% and rollback canary image while we triage. Can we do an emergency roll back safely? :warning:
dana-ml: I pushed a kernel fusion optimization for attention that landed in v2026.3 — it picks a fused attention kernel when seq_len > 1024 and batch_size >= 4 to improve throughput. It might create a slow path for edge batches where batching is small but seq_len high. This can blow up tail latencies when batching heuristics misclassify. I'm looking at the PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1426
aj-runtime: good catch. Two parallel mitigations: 1) fast rollback to v2026.2 for canary 2) short-term runtime flag to disable the fused attention kernel selection for canary. Which is faster? Rollback is atomic but affects metrics capture; flag is small change but needs build.
leo-sre: Also check scheduling/batching window config — v2026.3 bumped the batching window from 6ms -> 10ms to enable larger batches. That could increase latency for small requests. Pulling historical batching-distribution metrics now.
maria-support: customers asking for ETA. They're impacted in production. If rollback is possible we should do it ASAP and notify.
emma-oncall: I can initiate canary weight -> 0% in 2 mins. That will redirect traffic to stable pool. If rollback needed that'll take a couple deploy cycles. Which do you want first? 
aj-runtime: drop canary to 0% now to stop new incidents and preserve traces. We'll keep canary nodes up for logs/traces. After that we can decide rollback. 
emma-oncall: executing: canary-weight set 0% -> done. :white_check_mark: Traffic is back on stable.
leo-sre: initial observations: canary pods show increased batch wait time distribution — mean wait ~7.8ms vs 3.2ms on stable; but tails at 95/99 show spikes correlated with fused kernel selection events. Also GPU SM utilization looks fine; stalls not primary. KV cache miss rate slightly higher on canary (~6% -> 12%) but not enough to explain 9s p99.
dana-ml: that aligns with theory. The fused kernel seems to fall back to a slow reference path when conditions don't match perfectly. I can push a runtime flag to skip fused kernel selection in canary (hotfix) — small change, no model compile.
aj-runtime: ok do that. Please ensure flag default = off for canary. Also we should collect bisect candidates: PRs merged in the last 24h touching kernel selector, batching, or quantization. I'll list them.
aj-runtime: candidates: PR#1426 (attention kernel fusion) by dana-ml, PR#1431 (batching window change) by ryan-scheduler, PR#1438 (kv cache eviction tweak) by luca-cache. 
maria-support: for customer comms: I have a draft note: "We observed increased tail latency for some long-context workloads; we've moved affected traffic off the canary while we investigate and will update within 1 hour." Want me to send? 
emma-oncall: yes send and CC ops. Good to own comms while we triage. 
maria-support: sent to impacted customers, included trace IDs r-8f3b2/r-8f3b9 and link to support doc.
dana-ml: pushed hotfix flag: runtime config `attention.fused_enabled=false` for canary nodes. No build required, rolling config applied at 2351234585.
aj-runtime: monitoring dashboards: after disabling fused kernel, early signals look better — p95 dropped from 4.6s -> 2.3s in canary traces over the last 2 minutes. p99 still noisy, but trending down. 
leo-sre: continue to watch queue depth and kernel selector logs. Also we should run an isolated A/B synthetic: replay a sample load against v2026.3 with fused disabled vs enabled to quantify. I'll start replay job now.
aj-runtime: NJUMP repro steps for qa/sre to reproduce locally:
```
# small curl reproducer
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -d '{"model":"redwood-70b","input":"<~2k token prompt>","max_tokens":256}'
  -H "x-request-id: r-8f3b2"
```
Check response time and then inspect runtime logs on canary pod `rdw-rt-canary-012`:
```
rdwctl tail rdw-rt-canary-012 | grep "kernel-selector" -A 5
rdwctl metrics --pod rdw-rt-canary-012 | grep batch_wait_ms
```

leo-sre: replay job results: enabled vs disabled fused kernel under identical replay shows p99 drop from 8.9s -> 3.2s. p95 is similar to stable when fused disabled. Logs show many "selector_fallback_to_ref": true events when fused enabled.
aj-runtime: ok, decision: revert the fused kernel selection in mainline until we harden selection logic. We'll revert PR#1426 and publish a follow-up with improved heuristics. Also keep batching window change PR#1431 paused for now.
emma-oncall: planning rollback of PR#1426 and setting a postmortem ticket. Any blockers for revert? 
dana-ml: I'll open the revert PR and add better telemetry to the selector to avoid blind spots. Also will add unit tests for edge cases (batch sizes 1-3, seq_len > 1024). 
maria-support: customer comms updated: "We applied a mitigation and are rolling back a recent performance optimization that caused tail latency for a subset of long-context workloads. We're monitoring and will follow up in 2 hours with root cause and timeline." 
leo-sre: next actions: 1) confirm stable p95/p99 return to baseline over next 30m 2) run bisect if any residual tails 3) postmortem + RCA doc. Assigning tasks: aj-runtime -> revert PR & release, dana-ml -> telemetry + tests, leo-sre -> replay and monitoring, emma-oncall -> confirm canary weight reintroduce plan.
aj-runtime: I'll handle the revert and coordinate a patch release. ETA ~45m.
emma-oncall: I'll hold off on reintroducing canary until we add extra telemetry and gating. Reopening incident channel in 2 hrs for follow-ups. :lock:
maria-support: closing loop with customers now. Thanks all. Appreciate the quick triage. :heart:
